subject.title: fix(gateway): archive legacy-root stale transcript files on reset/delete

question: Should reset/delete accept a runtime archive candidate for stale legacy-root `.jsonl` paths under the OpenClaw-owned legacy sessions root with the current canonicalization and symlink-escape guard?
rationale: The patch is narrowly implemented and tested, but it deliberately changes which raw filesystem paths reset/delete may rename, so the final boundary choice belongs to a maintainer.

options.title: Accept bounded runtime archive
options.body: Merge after exact-head checks remain green because the helper canonicalizes both root and candidate and tests cover reset, delete, outside-root, and symlink-escape cases.

options.title: Require live command proof
options.body: Ask for one live `/clear` or `/reset` command transcript before merge if maintainers want command-dispatch proof beyond the archive-flow repro.

options.title: Defer to migration-only cleanup
options.body: Pause this PR if maintainers decide stale legacy transcript files should be handled only by doctor or migration code, not runtime reset/delete.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded runtime archive
recommendation.body: Merge after exact-head checks remain green because the helper canonicalizes both root and candidate and tests cover reset, delete, outside-root, and symlink-escape cases.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent blame and history make this the strongest routing candidate for the session path/archive boundary decision.
